body.statement: Using the sign-invariant affine-chart compiler handle, construct an algorithm that decides both directed cover relations for every finite input \(G,H,\mathcal I\), returns a finite certificate of the decision, and derives an explicit bit-operation bound as a displayed function of \(N\), \(|\mathcal I|\), and the rational input encoding length. Then enumerate the complete equivalence class inside the \(2^{N(N-1)}\) labeled digraph universe modulo latent relabeling. The construction must resolve punctured affine feasibility, Hall--Rado ranks, source partitions, nullification, and lower-dimensional chart incidences without returning unrestricted quantifier elimination as the answer.
body.justification: Effective finite comparison, including a size-dependent stopping bound, is the genuine open step separating a representation theorem from an existential reformulation.
body.gap: No located paper supplies an exact-support common-mechanism compiler; Dai et al. traverse an observational equivalence class using graph moves under a different support convention.
body.consumer: A graph-learning system can compile an intervention design once, compare candidates deterministically, and enumerate all observationally and interventionally indistinguishable hidden feedback structures.
